messages:
Alex W: Quick sync — long-term thinking about routing + multi-region + per-tenant isolation. I sketched a v1 approach: edge-affinity for low-latency reads, plus soft tenant-slices for isolation. We should decide what must be in v1 vs v2 (customer asks: AcmeBank wants strict data residency, RetailCo wants predictable throughput).

Maya N: +1 to edge-affinity concept. Can you define "tenant-slice" quickly?

Alex W: Tenant-slice = logical placement bucket (pool of GPUs) with isolation controls (network, routing policy, KV namespaces). Soft slice = shared pool with prioritization; hard slice = reserved capacity. v1 = soft slices + routing tags; v2 = hard reserved slices and strict tenancy.

Jorge R: From infra side: need routing policy rules that can express fallback + affinity. Suggest policy primitives: region_preference, tenant_affinity, capacity_floor, fallback_variant. Example policy format: 
```
policy {
  prefer: ["region:eu-west-1", "edge:eu" ]
  affinity: "tenant:acme"
  capacity_floor: 0.2
  fallback: ["model:small-quant", "region:us-west-2"]
}
```

Priya S: Data residency ask: AcmeBank requires that inference and KV cache live in EU only. Soft slices won't meet that. We need a clear launch criterion for any customer with residency requirements.

Tom C: Cost/ops note: soft slices + affinity reduces p99 latency but increases fragmentation. We should set a target cost-multiplier for v1 (e.g., <1.4x hosted baseline). If we blow past that, sales will push back.

Maya N: Agreed. Also define canary + rollback rules. My proposal: canary 5% traffic -> measure p99, error-rate, cost delta for 24h -> canary -> 25% -> full. Rollback triggers: error_rate > 1% OR p99 increase > 2x OR cost-multiplier > 2.0.

Jorge R: Ops checks: autoscaler must respect slice priority and capacity_floor. For multi-region: route-primary by region_preference, then affinity, then fallback. We need policy evaluation order documented.

Priya S: For AcmeBank to onboard in v1 we need: 1) region_restriction tag enforcement, 2) KMS-backed keys in-region, 3) audit logs for requests, 4) SLA doc. If any of these missing, it's v2.

Alex W: Good shading. So proposed v1 scope (minimum to launch a routing/tenancy feature):
- Policy evaluator & basic primitives (region_preference, tenant_affinity, fallback)
- Soft tenant slices with priority/weights
- Edge-affinity header + routing by edge region
- Canary automation + rollout config template
- Monitoring: token-level latency/cost + per-tenant SLO dashboard
- Docs + migration guide for customers
(Excludes: hard reserved slices, strict single-region enforcement, per-tenant hardware isolation)

Tom C: Launch metrics we should track: p99 latency, median latency, request error rate, cost per 1k tokens, slice fragmentation ratio. Set initial SLOs: p99 < 250ms for small models, error_rate < 0.5%.

Maya N: Customer-driven prioritization: if a paying enterprise (AcmeBank) signs for dedicated reservation, we escalate hard slice work earlier. Otherwise stick to v1 and monitor evictions/pressure.

Jorge R: Action items for infra team: 1) implement policy evaluator prototype (ETA 3w), 2) add region_preference routing to router (ETA 2w), 3) autoscaler respect capacity_floor (ETA 4w).

Priya S: Product/security action: draft residency checklist for customers (ETA 1w), and define acceptance criteria for in-region KMS (ETA 2w).

Alex W: I'll put together a short launch criteria doc and a decision matrix (v1 vs v2 triggers). Can we all review tomorrow at 11am? @Maya N @Jorge R @Priya S @Tom C :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deployment pipeline: new feature branch created for policy-evaluator (#feat/policy-eval). CI tests queued.

Tom C: :thumbsup: I'll prepare cost sims for both soft + hard slice scenarios.

Maya N: I'll draft the rollout template and canary playbook.

Alex W: Thanks — we'll keep scope tight for v1, ship primitives, and let customer demand drive hard-slice acceleration.
